newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat cites lack of U.S. pressure in peace crisis.
newsitem.headline: Arafat cites lack of U.S. pressure in peace crisis.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Monday the lack of American pressure on Israel had caused what one U.S. official described as a breakdown in Israeli-PLO peacemaking.

Asked to comment on remarks by Washington's ambassador to Israel that the "core bargain" of the 1993 Israel-PLO peace deal had broken down, Arafat told reporters in Gaza: "Because there is no American pressure to save the peace process."

U.S. Ambassador Martin Indyk said in remarks before the U.S.-Israel Chamber of Commerce on Sunday that the framework interim 1993 peace deal reached at Oslo between the PLO and Israel's former government had foundered.
"The core bargain of Oslo has broken down -- Israel was promised security and the Palestinians were promised self-government," Indyk said, as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu listened.

U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross failed after a nine-day mission that ended last week to revive Israeli-PLO peace talks, frozen since Israel launched construction on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Arafat, disappointed with Ross's performance during the nine-day mission, asked U.S. President Bill Clinton in a letter sent on Thursday, to personally get involved in efforts to break the impasse.
